h: Getting the Most From Your Minutes in the Air
p: The single best bit of advice for first-time flyers? Relax. It sounds daft when there's a gale roaring under you, but tense, rigid bodies wobble about, while loose, calm ones float. Keep your chin up, your hips pushed forward and your arms soft, and trust the instructor to do the steering.

A few practical bits help too. Take off watches, rings and earrings before you go in, empty your pockets completely and wear trainers that lace up properly, because anything loose in the tunnel becomes a problem. Contact lenses and glasses are worth mentioning to the team when you arrive. Get there with plenty of time for check-in and the training video, and don't eat a huge meal just before you fly.

Many centres also offer the chance to watch the instructors show off with a high-speed demo, and seeing them zip up and down the tunnel is half the entertainment for whoever's watching through the glass. Photos and videos are usually available too, if you want proof you really did it.

Manchester is brilliant for filling the rest of the day. Football fans can take a tour at Old Trafford or the Etihad, and the National Football Museum in the city centre is a treat for anyone who loves the game. The John Rylands Research Institute and Library on Deansgate is a stunning neo-Gothic building that looks like it belongs at Hogwarts, and the Science and Industry Museum in Castlefield tells the story of the city that kicked off the Industrial Revolution.
